about: Limits for CI's Size budget job (scripts/size_budget.py, whose top comment has the detail). Flash (the OTA image) has no cap here: a build fails over 90% of its OTA slot (read from the partition table in the build's factory image), and needs the owner's approval when it has grown more than release.allowance_flash since release.tag, or when one pull request adds more than 32 KB. release holds each build's flash at the last release; run `python3 scripts/size_budget.py release-baseline <sizes> <tag>` when a release is cut, never by hand. firmware.static_ram (internal data RAM from the ELF, ESPHome's RAM line) and host.heap (tests/heap_budget.cpp, internal RAM on the panel) are tight absolute caps: going over fails, and a pull request that raises one needs the owner's approval, so raise only the entry that needs it and add the reason to this text. JSON documents (PSRAM on the panel) have no cap, only max_growth.json. max_growth: the most one pull request may add to a figure against the base branch. The owner approves with a commit status on the pull request: context budget/owner-approval, state success, description `approved static_ram=<B> heap=<B> flash=<B>`. Approval passes only those approval items, never the 90% limit or a cap overrun. 2026-11-03: season_nhl heap cap added. 2026-11-08: this scheme replaced the hand-set flash and JSON caps; release seeded from v2026.11.0's build. A change that moves the release block to another tag must name a later vYYYY.M.P tag whose Build run measured exactly the baseline figures given, or it fails.
